introduction: This chapter tells the story of the Kalbeliya people, traditional snake charmers in India. It explores their deep connection with snakes, their traditional knowledge of medicines, and how their lives have changed due to new laws protecting wildlife.
keyTakeaways: Kalbeliyas are traditional snake charmers who regard snakes as family treasures.
Snakes play a vital role in farming by controlling the rat population.
Most snakes are not poisonous; only four types in India are highly venomous.
The government has banned catching wild animals to protect them from exploitation.
Kalbeliyas now use their musical talents for new types of entertainment while preserving their heritage.
revisionNotes: Focus on the 4 types of poisonous snakes, the role of Been, and the Kalbeliya heritage. Understand the impact of the Wildlife Protection Act.
